questions.question: Which property most clearly distinguishes SRAM used in on-chip caches from DRAM used as external memory in accelerators for inference?
questions.choice_A: SRAM has lower latency and higher area cost per bit compared to DRAM
questions.choice_B: SRAM has significantly higher density than DRAM at the same technology node
questions.choice_C: DRAM supports random access while SRAM does not
questions.choice_D: DRAM consumes less energy per access than SRAM at the same bandwidth

questions.question: In autoregressive decoding with a KV cache, what is the primary reason decoding scales roughly linearly in time per token after the prefill phase (assuming full attention and no retrieval)?
questions.choice_A: The model re-encodes all previous tokens at each step
questions.choice_B: The KV cache allows skipping recomputation for past tokens; attention only attends to stored keys/values
questions.choice_C: The softmax is precomputed for all possible queries
questions.choice_D: The embedding lookup amortizes compute across steps

questions.question: Which factor most often becomes the bottleneck when context length grows very large and the KV cache no longer fits in on-chip memory?
questions.choice_A: Compute throughput for matrix multiplications
questions.choice_B: Disk I/O bandwidth
questions.choice_C: Memory bandwidth to stream keys/values from off-chip memory
questions.choice_D: Latency of positional encoding computation

questions.question: How does increasing context length affect prefill latency for a standard full-attention Transformer without architectural changes?
questions.choice_A: Prefill latency grows quadratically with context length due to attention score computation
questions.choice_B: Prefill latency remains constant because attention caches are reused
questions.choice_C: Prefill latency grows logarithmically due to softmax normalization
questions.choice_D: Prefill latency decreases because longer sequences improve tensor core utilization

questions.question: What is a key difference between Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) with respect to KV cache footprint?
questions.choice_A: MQA stores one key and one value per head group, while GQA stores one per group where group size > 1; MQA tends to minimize KV size the most
questions.choice_B: GQA stores one key per head but many values per head; MQA stores many keys per head but one value
questions.choice_C: GQA eliminates the KV cache entirely; MQA requires a full KV cache
questions.choice_D: Both MQA and GQA increase KV cache size relative to multi-head attention

questions.question: Why might activation (and KV) quantization to 4–8 bits provide larger end-to-end latency improvements at long context lengths compared to short ones?
questions.choice_A: Quantization increases arithmetic intensity, which is more helpful when compute-bound
questions.choice_B: Quantization reduces memory footprint and bandwidth demand, which dominates at long contexts
questions.choice_C: Quantization removes the need for softmax, which dominates long-context cost
questions.choice_D: Quantization enables weight tying across layers, reducing parameter count

questions.question: Which mitigation technique reduces KV cache growth without changing the base model weights and can preserve near-full quality on tasks focusing on recent context?
questions.choice_A: Sliding-window (local) attention that evicts or ignores distant tokens
questions.choice_B: Increasing the number of attention heads
questions.choice_C: Replacing softmax with ReLU
questions.choice_D: Adding extra feed-forward layers

questions.question: When deploying on-device (e.g., mobile) inference, which memory characteristic most strongly argues for aggressive KV cache compression compared to server GPUs?
questions.choice_A: On-device SRAM has lower latency than server SRAM
questions.choice_B: On-device DRAM capacity and bandwidth are much more limited, making KV traffic a larger fraction of the budget
questions.choice_C: On-device processors have more tensor cores to hide memory latency
questions.choice_D: Server GPUs cannot use quantized activations

questions.question: What is a practical consequence of placing the KV cache in host DRAM over PCIe instead of GPU HBM for very long contexts?
questions.choice_A: Higher arithmetic precision
questions.choice_B: Substantially increased per-token latency due to interconnect bandwidth and latency constraints
questions.choice_C: Reduced memory fragmentation on the GPU
questions.choice_D: Guaranteed throughput improvements from overlapping computation

questions.question: Which statement best describes the difference between latency and throughput implications of longer contexts in batched decoding?
questions.choice_A: Latency per token increases, but throughput per accelerator always increases
questions.choice_B: Both latency per token and throughput per accelerator decrease due to higher memory bandwidth pressure
questions.choice_C: Latency per token increases, and throughput can decrease if the workload becomes bandwidth-bound
questions.choice_D: Latency per token decreases, but throughput per accelerator also decreases

questions.question: Why is careful memory layout (e.g., block-wise or paged KV caches) helpful for long-context inference with dynamic sequence lengths and batching?
questions.choice_A: It prevents the need for positional encodings
questions.choice_B: It reduces numerical error in softmax
questions.choice_C: It minimizes fragmentation and enables efficient reuse/eviction of KV blocks across heterogeneous sequences
questions.choice_D: It halves the number of attention heads required

questions.question: Which compression approach is most aligned with preserving attention geometry while reducing KV cache size?
questions.choice_A: Random subsampling of tokens in the cache
questions.choice_B: Low-rank projection or product quantization of K and V tensors per head
questions.choice_C: Dropping the value cache and recomputing values on the fly
questions.choice_D: Replacing attention with a convolution kernel

questions.question: In a server-side multi-GPU deployment, sharding the KV cache across devices primarily trades off which resources?
questions.choice_A: Local compute for global memory bandwidth
questions.choice_B: On-device memory capacity for interconnect bandwidth/latency between devices
questions.choice_C: DRAM capacity for SSD capacity
questions.choice_D: Model parameters for activations

questions.question: What is the main benefit of FlashAttention-style kernels to long-context inference when the KV cache resides in HBM?
questions.choice_A: They reduce the asymptotic complexity of attention from quadratic to linear
questions.choice_B: They improve IO efficiency via tiling and on-chip SRAM reuse, reducing HBM traffic for attention
questions.choice_C: They eliminate the need for a KV cache during decoding
questions.choice_D: They increase batch size by quantizing weights

questions.question: Which scenario most likely becomes compute-bound rather than memory-bound at long contexts?
questions.choice_A: Small models with high batch sizes running on bandwidth-limited devices
questions.choice_B: Large models with few heads and low precision activations
questions.choice_C: Very large models with high head counts and large hidden sizes on high-bandwidth GPUs, during prefill
questions.choice_D: Any model using MQA or GQA

questions.question: Which statement about the scaling of KV cache memory with context length T is most accurate for multi-head attention with H heads and hidden size d?
questions.choice_A: KV memory is O(T d) and independent of H
questions.choice_B: KV memory is O(T H d_head) where d_head = d/H; net scaling is O(T d)
questions.choice_C: KV memory is O(T^2 d) due to pairwise interactions
questions.choice_D: KV memory is O(H^2 T) due to head cross-terms

questions.question: What is a typical accuracy-risk trade-off when quantizing the KV cache to 4-bit while keeping compute in higher precision (e.g., FP16)?
questions.choice_A: No measurable impact on any task
questions.choice_B: Potential degradation on tasks requiring precise long-range dependencies or rare-token disambiguation
questions.choice_C: Instability during training convergence
questions.choice_D: Inability to decode single-token outputs

questions.question: Why might retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigate the need for extremely large contiguous KV caches in long-context applications?
questions.choice_A: RAG compresses the KV cache using autoencoders
questions.choice_B: RAG replaces attention with nearest-neighbor search in the embedding space
questions.choice_C: RAG lets the model attend over a small window plus injected retrieved snippets, reducing the need to retain the entire prior context
questions.choice_D: RAG forces the model to ignore all context beyond 512 tokens

questions.question: For on-device inference, which design choice often yields the best energy-efficiency improvement at long contexts under strict memory constraints?
questions.choice_A: Increasing core frequency to reduce latency
questions.choice_B: Using MQA/GQA plus 4–8 bit KV cache quantization to reduce memory traffic
questions.choice_C: Doubling the number of attention heads
questions.choice_D: Switching to larger models for better utilization

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when scaling batch size for higher throughput during long-context decoding?
questions.choice_A: Batching eliminates data parallelism in the model
questions.choice_B: Larger batches reduce arithmetic intensity
questions.choice_C: Batching can saturate memory bandwidth with KV reads, causing diminishing or negative throughput gains
questions.choice_D: Batching forces weights to be reloaded every step

questions.question: Which latency optimization is most specific to the decode phase in long-context inference and less impactful in prefill?
questions.choice_A: CUDA graph capture of static decode loops to reduce launch overhead
questions.choice_B: Mixed-precision GEMMs in attention score computation
questions.choice_C: Model distillation to a smaller teacher
questions.choice_D: Increasing sequence length to improve occupancy
